technology_name: Monoclonal Antibodies for Detecting and Blocking Viral Infections
problem_solved: Lack of highly specific diagnostic tools and targeted therapeutics to rapidly detect and neutralize emerging and re-emerging viral threats.
description: A pipeline for developing monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) using hybridoma technology. BALB/c mice are immunized with viral structural proteins via plasmid-based gene delivery. Upon optimal IgG response, splenocytes are fused with myeloma cells, selected via HAT medium, and subcloned to establish stable monoclones. The mAbs undergo functional characterization (Western blot, immunofluorescence) and epitope mapping to pinpoint critical antigenic sites, establishing a foundation for neutralizing therapeutic antibodies and advanced diagnostic assays.
applications:
• Commercial manufacturing of rapid viral diagnostic kits and ELISA reagents

• Therapeutic monoclonal antibody design for neutralizing viral infections

• National biodefense stockpiling and outbreak surveillance programs

• Commercial out-licensing to global pharmaceutical and clinical diagnostic companies
